conceptual assets.information: The 32-bit lock ownership and availability state held by the spinlock array; spinlock operation depends on it to record which locks are held and to report their status.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The selected lock_q bit is changed from bus_req_i.rw on line 45, so an unauthorized bus request can modify lock state. A lock can be left asserted by the assignment on line 45, preventing clients from acquiring it and blocking synchronized operation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue a bus request that sets a lock and keep it asserted, corrupting ownership and preventing legitimate clients from acquiring that lock.

conceptual assets.information: The decoded selection of which of the 32 lock entries a per-lock access addresses; it determines which lock state is changed and which selected status bit contributes to the response.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: bus_req_i.addr determines sel on line 51, and sel determines which lock_q entry may change on line 44, so changing the address can redirect a lock operation. The selection gates lock updates on line 44 and masks the per-lock response on line 68, so an attacker can prevent or misroute the intended lock access.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could present an address selecting another lock or no valid lock, redirecting acquisition or release and preventing the intended lock transaction.

considered, not kept.concept: Bus response handshake and error status
considered, not kept.reason: The acknowledge only copies bus_req_i.stb and the error field is assigned a constant on lines 63-65, so these fields are handshake or constant status rather than security-relevant information.
Clock and reset inputs are excluded conceptual assets, and lines 41-43 and 60-62 only use them to time or reset the lock and response state.

reply keys: the 2026-10-13 format as written in 'raw'; 'reply' holds it in v5 keys
